overall_summary: Performance analysis of recent uploads reveals that space and astronomical anomaly content—specifically 'What If' hypothetical scenarios involving extreme planetary conditions and planetary phenomena—significantly outperforms general psychology, standard animal facts, or slower-paced historical storytelling. Videos published within the last 7 days focusing on planetary extremes (e.g., Venus day/year lengths, liquid diamond planets, extreme dark worlds) show dramatically higher views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes-per-view) compared to older or alternative subject matter. Audience engagement spikes when astronomical concepts are framed as tactile, dangerous, or experiential 'What If' scenarios.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Darkest Planet?' (YlDuGu1vzAg) generated high view velocity (over 800-1000 views rapidly) with strong like ratios (up to 38 likes).
winning_patterns.action: Double down on hypothetical immersive space scenarios involving extreme physical environments (e.g., falling into, landing on, or experiencing bizarre planetary anomalies).

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) achieved top-tier performance with ~1,000 views and strong audience retention signals.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more content highlighting counter-intuitive cosmic facts where standard physics or time scales are completely inverted.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos covering psychological tricks or basic brain trivia (e.g., 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories', 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head') consistently underperformed, pulling low view counts (5 to 71 views) and virtually zero comments.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standard human psychology and repetitive brain-hack facts for the immediate content schedule.

weak_patterns.pattern: Basic Animal Trivia Without a Twist
weak_patterns.evidence: Simple declarative animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (when published outside high-performing clusters) or general biological statements received modest traction compared to space anomalies.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid standard textbook animal facts unless framed inside a dramatic cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary mystery context.
